title: The Best SBA Lenders for Business Acquisitions Fit Your Deal
summary: The best SBA acquisition lenders have PLP authority and recent deals like yours. Rankings show volume, not fit, so compare several offers.
body_markdown:
The best SBA lenders for business acquisitions are active 7(a) lenders with Preferred Lender Program (PLP) authority and acquisition experience. They have closed recent change-of-ownership deals at your size and in your industry and underwrite to SOP 50 10 8.1, effective October 1, 2026. No single lender is best for every buyer, because volume rankings measure activity and leave fit unanswered.


Rankings also conflict from site to site, so treat them as a starting point. Live Oak says SBA named it the most active 7(a) lender by dollar amount in FY2025, per[Live Oak's FY2025 announcement](https://investor.liveoak.bank/news/news-details/2025/Live-Oak-Bank-Leads-Nation-in-SBA-7a-Lending-Activity/default.aspx) . Live Oak reports 2,280 approvals and more than $2.8 billion, a figure that covers every 7(a) loan purpose and reflects scale rather than acquisition fit.


This guide explains the acquisition rules as of November 2026, what lender rankings actually measure, and why PLP status matters. It then gives you an editorial framework for choosing a lender, avoiding common declines, and comparing offers efficiently.


### How SBA 7(a) Acquisition Loans Work in 2026


The SBA 7(a) program is the go-to option for buying a business. It finances changes of ownership, including goodwill, with long terms and a modest equity requirement. The acquisition rules changed three times since mid-2025: on June 1, 2025, March 1, 2026, and October 1, 2026.


Everything below reflects the rules as of November 2026, and the equity and eligibility sections detail each change with its SBA source. For a broader look at what shifted this year, see our breakdown of[SBA program changes in 2026](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-loan-program-changes-2026) .


#### Loan Limits, Terms, and Rate Caps


The U.S. Small Business Administration's page on[SBA 7(a) loan terms](https://www.sba.gov/sba-lenders/) says most 7(a) loans max out at $5 million. The same page lists changes of ownership, complete or partial, as an eligible use. Loans made under SBA Express have a lower maximum of $500,000.


Terms are generally 10 years or less, and terms of up to 25 years apply only to real estate. A business acquisition without property usually runs on the shorter schedule.


SBA guarantees up to 85% of loans of $150,000 or less and up to 75% of larger loans. Lenders set the rate, but SBA caps the variable rate by loan size. The base rate is pegged to prime or an SBA optional peg rate.


Loan amount Maximum variable rate (as of November 2026)


$50,000 or less Base rate plus 6.5%


$50,001 to $250,000 Base rate plus 6.0%


$250,001 to $350,000 Base rate plus 4.5%


Greater than $350,000 Base rate plus 3.0%


Most acquisition loans exceed $350,000, so the cap that usually applies is base rate plus 3.0%. SBA publishes fixed-rate maximums separately, so confirm any fixed-rate offer against SBA's current schedule before you sign.


#### Equity Injection and Seller Notes


The U.S. Small Business Administration's current rulebook,[SBA SOP 50 10 8.1](https://legacy.sba.gov/document/sop-50-10-lender-development-company-loan-programs) , sorts acquisition deals into four types. They are Initial Acquisition, Business Expansion, Owner Buyout, and ESOP & Cooperative.


An Initial Acquisition, where the buyer is new to the business, requires an equity injection of at least 10% of total project cost. For this deal type, the requirement cannot be reduced or eliminated.


Total project cost means all costs required to become operational, regardless of funding source, except lines of credit and 504 loans. On a $2 million project, that puts the minimum injection at $200,000.


Seller notes help, but only under strict conditions:


- **Full standby:** The seller note must be subordinated to the lender, with no principal or interest payments for the entire 7(a) term.
- **Half-of-injection cap:** Standby seller debt and minority-investor equity together can supply no more than half of the required injection.
- **Buyer's own funds:** At least half of the injection must come from the buyer's own sources, such as unborrowed cash.
- **Later refinancing:** Seller debt in a change-of-ownership deal can be refinanced once it has been in place and current for 36 months.


In the $2 million example, a full-standby seller note can cover up to $100,000. The buyer must bring at least $100,000 from their own sources.


The 10% minimum is not new, as the[SBA information notice on 8.1](https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/SBA%20Information%20Notice%205000-880695%20-%20Issuance%20of%20SOP%2050%2010%208.1.pdf) from the U.S. Small Business Administration explains. SBA reintroduced it on June 1, 2025, and carried it into 8.1 on October 1, 2026.


#### Eligibility and Underwriting Thresholds


Since March 1, 2026, all direct and indirect owners and SBA-required guarantors must be U.S. citizens or nationals living in the U.S. or its territories. The U.S. Small Business Administration's[SBA citizenship eligibility notice](https://www.naggl.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/5000-876626.pdf) , hosted by NAGGL, lists lawful permanent residents (green-card holders) as ineligible. Buyers relying on earlier guidance that allowed green-card holders need to recheck their ownership structure.


SOP 50 10 8.1 also sets three underwriting thresholds that shape acquisition deals:


- **Quality of Earnings:** A purchase price of $3 million or more requires a Quality of Earnings report in addition to the business valuation.
- **Valuation gap:** If the purchase price exceeds the valuation, the buyer must cover the difference with equity.
- **Debt service coverage:** An Initial Acquisition needs a minimum ratio of 1.25:1. For example, $400,000 in annual debt service needs $500,000 in cash flow.


### What Lender Rankings Tell You and What They Leave Out


In[SBA's FY2025 lending announcement](https://www.sba.gov/article/2025/09/30/trump-sba-delivers-record-capital-small-businesses-fy25) on September 30, 2025, the U.S. Small Business Administration said it had backed about 77,600 7(a) loans for $37 billion. That figure covers the prior fiscal year, which ended that day. At that scale, rankings help you see which lenders are most active.


Rankings are built from SBA volume data, so they measure total 7(a) activity across every loan purpose, including working capital, real estate, and refinancing. None of the public rankings isolate change-of-ownership loans, which means a high rank does not prove acquisition expertise.


How a ranking is sorted also changes the story it tells:


- **Deal count:** A high loan count can reflect many small loans rather than complex acquisitions.
- **Dollar volume:** A high dollar total can come from a few large real estate deals.
- **Average loan size:** This figure shows where a lender is comfortable, but it hides the range of deals it closes.


Different sites also report different numbers for the same lender, which is why the Live Oak figure above is attributed to the company. Use rankings to build a shortlist, then test each lender against your deal. Lenders face the same challenge from the other side, as our[SBA lending software guide](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-lending-software-how-to-choose-a-platform-that-speeds-decisions-without-adding-headcount) explains.


### Why Preferred Lender Program Status Matters


Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute publishes the[Preferred Lenders Program regulation](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/13/120.450) , 13 CFR § 120.450. Under it, designated lenders process, close, and service SBA loans with reduced documentation and without SBA prior approval. In short, a PLP lender holds delegated authority to approve your loan itself.


Loans from lenders without delegated authority, or deals a lender chooses not to process under it, go to SBA's Loan Guaranty Processing Center for review. In that case SBA reviews the loan before approval, so ask each lender a direct question: "Will you process my acquisition under your PLP authority?"


PLP status describes how a loan gets approved, and it says nothing about the price of the loan. Brokers who place acquisition deals regularly can also learn how lenders structure partnerships in our guide to[SBA lender referral programs](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-lender-broker-referral-programs-how-they-work-and-how-to-win) .


### How to Choose the Right SBA Lender for Your Acquisition


The framework below is editorial guidance from Lendflow, based on the SBA rules above and on how acquisition deals move through underwriting. It is meant to help you match a lender to your deal, and it does not rank individual lenders.


Work through each step in order: pick the right lender type, compare the all-in cost, and then collect several offers in one process.


#### Match the Lender Type to Your Deal


Each type of SBA lender brings different strengths to an acquisition. Use this table to decide where to start your search.


Lender type Typical strength Considerations


National SBA-focused lenders High 7(a) volume and familiarity with acquisition structures across many industries Process can feel standardized, so confirm they lend at your deal size


Regional and community banks Local market knowledge and a deposit relationship after closing Appetite for goodwill-heavy deals varies, so ask about recent acquisitions


Credit unions Member relationship and a local focus SBA activity varies widely, so confirm 7(a) volume and PLP status


Non-bank SBA lenders Business model centered on SBA and other government-guaranteed lending Confirm who services the loan and whether you need a separate bank for deposits


Within any type, the deciding factor is recent change-of-ownership experience at your size and in your industry. Ask for that directly, since SBA's public lender data does not break it out.


#### Compare the All-In Cost of Every Offer


Each 7(a) rate equals a base rate plus a lender-set spread, up to the SBA caps shown earlier. SBA also charges an upfront guaranty fee on the guaranteed portion of the loan. The U.S. Small Business Administration's[SOP 50 10 8.1 fee rules](https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx) permit the 7(a) lender to pass that fee to you.


The U.S. Small Business Administration sets the current schedule in[SBA's FY2027 7(a) fee notice](https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-09/Info%20Notice%20-%207(a)%20Fees%20FY%202027%20.pdf) , Information Notice 5000-881797, effective October 1, 2026. For loans of $700,001 to $5 million, the fee is 3.5% of the guaranteed portion up to $1 million, plus 3.75% of the portion over $1 million. The schedule changes each fiscal year, so confirm the current notice before you close.


Here is how that works on a $2 million loan with a 75% guarantee. The guaranteed portion is $1.5 million, so the fee is $35,000 on the first $1 million plus $18,750 on the rest. That adds up to $53,750.


The same SBA notice states that lenders may not pass the lender's annual service fee on to the borrower. When you compare offers side by side, line up the spread, the index, any packaging or closing fees, and who pays the guaranty fee.

### Common Reasons SBA Acquisition Loans Get Declined


Most acquisition declines trace back to rules that buyers can check before applying. Review this list against your deal before you submit it to any lender:


- **Equity gap:** The buyer cannot show 10% of total project cost from eligible sources, or too much comes from standby debt.
- **Seller note not on full standby:** A note with any scheduled payments during the 7(a) term does not count toward equity.
- **Ownership eligibility:** An owner or required guarantor is not a U.S. citizen or U.S. national with a U.S. principal residence.
- **Low debt service coverage:** Projected cash flow falls below 1.25:1 for an Initial Acquisition.
- **Price above valuation:** The purchase price exceeds the business valuation and the buyer has not added equity to cover the difference.
- **Missing Quality of Earnings:** A deal priced at $3 million or more lacks the required Quality of Earnings report.
- **Stale documents:** SBA's SOP 50 10 8.1 requires guarantor personal financial statements dated within 90 days of approval. Non-delegated loans need credit reports within 90 days.
- **Incomplete financials:** SOP 50 10 8.1 adds more detailed requirements for reviewing historical and interim financial information, so incomplete financials slow review.


Most of these issues are fixable when caught early. Use our checklist of[SBA loan document requirements](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-loan-software-for-small-businesses-features-compliance-and-how-to-choose) to build a complete package before the first lender sees it.


### Questions to Ask Every SBA Lender Before You Apply


The right questions reveal fit faster than any ranking. Ask every lender on your shortlist the same set so you can compare answers directly:


- **PLP authority:** Will you process my acquisition under your PLP delegated authority?
- **Acquisition track record:** How many change-of-ownership deals at my size and in my industry did you close recently?
- **Rate structure:** What spread and index will you use, and do you offer a fixed rate?
- **Fees:** Which fees, including the SBA guaranty fee, will you pass to me?
- **Seller note:** How will you treat my seller note, and will you require full standby?
- **Equity and timeline:** What equity injection will you require, and what is your expected timeline to close?
- **Servicing:** Who services the loan after closing, and who will be my point of contact?


The servicing answer matters for the life of the loan. Learn[how SBA loan servicing works](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-loan-servicing-how-it-works-for-borrowers-and-lenders) before you choose.


### FAQs


#### Can You Get an SBA Loan for a Business Acquisition?


Yes, changes of ownership are an eligible use of SBA 7(a) loans. Approval still depends on meeting the equity injection, ownership eligibility, and underwriting rules in SOP 50 10 8.1.


#### How Much Down Payment Do I Need for an SBA Acquisition Loan?


An initial acquisition requires at least 10% of total project cost as of November 2026. Up to half of that injection can come from a seller note on full standby for the life of the 7(a) loan.


#### What Is the 20% Rule for SBA Loans?


The 20% rule commonly refers to SBA's requirement that individuals owning 20% or more of the borrower provide a personal guarantee. Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute publishes the[SBA personal guarantee regulation](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/13/120.160) , which says holders of at least 20% generally must guarantee the loan.


#### Which SBA Lender Has the Lowest Interest Rates?


No single lender has the lowest rates, because each lender sets its own spread up to SBA's caps. Compare several offers on both the rate and the fees passed to you.


#### What Is the Maximum SBA 7(a) Loan Amount for Buying a Business?


Most 7(a) loans, including acquisition loans, have a maximum of $5 million. SBA Express loans are capped at $500,000.


#### Are SBA Loan Rates the Same at Every Lender?


No, SBA sets maximum rates while each lender sets its own spread within them. Two lenders can offer different rates on the same deal.
